definitions.primary_positive: The primary conversational act is payment_proposal: putting forward future payment or revised payment-component terms. No authority, validity, final acceptance, permission, or complete wording is required.
definitions.primary_negative: A different known primary conversational act; payment may be background, conditional discussion, disavowed, past, or secondary.
definitions.primary_ambiguous: Dominant act cannot be recovered with sufficient confidence from permitted source snapshots, roles, questions and referents. observed_binary is false and binary_value is null.
definitions.primary_component_answers: A response supplying new or repaired payment amounts/dates can be a descriptive payment_proposal. Merely confirming an unchanged offer or readback is a response act. Exact repetition with unclear acceptance/proposal intent is masked.
definitions.act_completion: Completion of the identifiable primary act as expressed, separate from semantic class and valid terms. Explicit open words or qualifications can make a recognizable proposal unfinished. Missing required policy fields alone do not make a descriptive act unfinished.
definitions.date_label: Completion only of the current semantic date expression, including a period or relation. Complete can be vague, unresolved, rejected, quoted, conditional, or calendar-invalid. No semantic date span would be ambiguous and unobserved, with value_resolution unknown; absence would not be asserted.
definitions.date_multi_target: Preserve candidate status for each requested target. If target candidates have different completion statuses, mask the record-wide label as ambiguous. Discarded fragments do not override a completed replacement, and discarded complete dates do not override an unfinished replacement.
definitions.predicate_polarity: Affirmative or negated describes the local source predicate associating/reporting/selecting or rejecting the date. This is not a payment commitment or permission. Reporting, quotation, and conditional applicability are separately preserved in expression_context.

value_resolution.exact: Full calendar specificity is explicitly expressed, or a unique supplied spoken referent resolves the complete expression. No new normalized date is generated.
value_resolution.vague: A complete expression leaves date granularity, year, date format, alternative choice or calendar anchoring unspecified.
value_resolution.reference_unresolved: A complete anaphoric/relational expression lacks a unique supplied referent.
value_resolution.invalid: Fully expressed calendar terms are inconsistent or nonexistent.
value_resolution.unknown: Insufficient expression or mixed candidate status prevents assigning one resolution.

definitions.span_offsets: Zero-based, end-exclusive Unicode code points in the parsed UTF-8 source string field. JSON pointers bind to the actual input packet. Additional UTF-8 byte offsets refer to that decoded field encoded as UTF-8, not whole-file byte positions.
